title: Wave 5 Person-by-Person India (Epics, Maurya, Gupta, Tibet, Lanka), Imperial China/Korea, Abulghazi Turks/Seljuks, Celtic Milesians, Normandy & Kievan Rus'

nodes.name: Lord Rama / Sri Ramachandra (Gen 65, Son of Dasharatha; Hero of Ramayana)
nodes.notes: Eldest son of King Dasharatha & Kausalya; husband of Sita; father of Lava & Kusha.

nodes.name: Goddess Sita / Janaki (Daughter of Siradhvaja Janaka; Queen of Ayodhya)
nodes.role: Princess of Videha & Mother of Lava and Kusha
nodes.notes: Daughter of King Siradhvaja Janaka; mother of twins Lava and Kusha.

nodes.name: Prince Bharata (Son of Dasharatha & Kaikeyi; Regent of Ayodhya)
nodes.notes: Ruled Ayodhya from Nandigrama bearing Rama's sandals during the 14-year exile.

nodes.name: Prince Lakshmana (Son of Dasharatha & Sumitra; Companion of Rama)
nodes.notes: Accompanied Rama & Sita throughout the 14-year forest exile.

nodes.name: Prince Shatrughna (Son of Dasharatha & Sumitra; Founder of Mathura's Solar Line)
nodes.notes: Conquered Lavana and founded Mathura.

nodes.name: King Lava of Shravasti (Twin Son of Rama & Sita; Ancestor of Mewar Sisodias)
nodes.role: Twin Prince of North Kosala & Lahore
nodes.notes: Traditional Solar ancestor of North Kosala / Shravasti and Mewar Rajputs.

nodes.name: King Kusha of Kushavati (Twin Son of Rama & Sita; Ancestor of Brihadbala)
nodes.role: Twin Prince Continuing Ayodhya Main Line
nodes.notes: Father of Atithi, continuing the Ayodhya Solar Dynasty to Brihadbala.

nodes.name: Emperor Yudhishthira (Eldest Pandava; Dharmaraja of Indraprastha)
nodes.notes: Victor of Kurukshetra & Emperor of Hastinapura.

nodes.name: Prince Bhima / Bhimasena (2nd Pandava; Slayer of Jarasandha & Duryodhana)
nodes.notes: Father of Ghatotkacha.

nodes.name: Prince Arjuna (3rd Pandava; Recipient of the Bhagavad Gita; Ancestor of Parikshit)
nodes.notes: Wed Draupadi and Subhadra (sister of Krishna); father of Abhimanyu.

nodes.name: Prince Nakula (4th Pandava; Twin Son of Pandu & Madri)
nodes.notes: Master of horses and swords.

nodes.name: Prince Sahadeva (5th Pandava; Twin Son of Pandu & Madri)
nodes.notes: Scholar-warrior of the Pandavas.

nodes.name: Crown Prince Duryodhana (Eldest of 100 Kauravas; Son of Dhritarashtra & Gandhari)
nodes.notes: Eldest son of Dhritarashtra & Gandhari.

nodes.name: Prince Abhimanyu (Son of Arjuna & Subhadra; Father of Parikshit)
nodes.notes: Fell at the Chakravyuha; married Uttara and fathered posthumous heir Parikshit.

nodes.name: Emperor Parikshit (Son of Abhimanyu & Uttara; Sole Surviving Kuru Heir)
nodes.notes: Saved in the womb by Krishna; father of Janamejaya.

nodes.name: Emperor Janamejaya (Son of Parikshit; Patron of Mahabharata Recitation)
nodes.notes: Heard the Mahabharata recited by Vaishampayana.

nodes.name: Emperor Chandragupta Maurya (Founder of Maurya Empire, r. 322–297 BCE)
nodes.role: Unifier of India & Ally/Father-in-Law of Seleucus I
nodes.notes: Overthrew the Nandas with Chanakya and forged a treaty with Seleucus I Nicator.

nodes.name: Emperor Bindusara Amitraghata (Son of Chandragupta Maurya, r. 297–273 BCE)
nodes.role: Father of Ashoka & Correspondent of Antiochus I
nodes.notes: Extended Mauryan rule south across the Deccan.

nodes.name: Emperor Ashoka the Great (r. 268–232 BCE; Pillar Edicts Naming Antiochus II & Ptolemy II)
nodes.notes: Sent Buddhist missions to Sri Lanka, Syria, Egypt, and Macedonia.

nodes.name: Arahant Mahinda & Therī Sanghamitta (Son & Daughter of Ashoka Who Brought Buddhism to Lanka)
nodes.notes: Brought the Bodhi Tree sapling to Anuradhapura under King Devanampiya Tissa.

nodes.name: Maharaja Sri Gupta (Founder of Gupta Line, c. 240–280 CE)
nodes.notes: Father of Ghatotkacha Gupta.

nodes.name: Maharajadhiraja Chandragupta I (r. 319–335 CE; + Licchavi Princess Kumaradevi)
nodes.notes: Allied with the ancient Licchavis of Vaisali through Kumaradevi.

nodes.name: Emperor Samudragupta (Son of Chandragupta I, r. 335–375 CE; Allahabad Pillar)
nodes.notes: Extended Gupta suzerainty from Himalayas to South India.

nodes.name: Emperor Chandragupta II Vikramaditya (Son of Samudragupta, r. 375–415 CE)
nodes.notes: Overthrew the Western Kshatrapas and hosted Chinese pilgrim Faxian.

nodes.name: Emperor Kumaragupta I (Son of Chandragupta II, r. 415–455 CE; Founder of Nalanda Mahavihara)
nodes.notes: Founded the great monastic university of Nalanda.

nodes.name: Emperor Skandagupta (Son of Kumaragupta I, r. 455–467 CE; Repelled Huna Invasions)
nodes.notes: Defeated the Hephthalites (White Huns) in northern India.

nodes.name: King Vijaya of Tambapanni (1st King of Sri Lanka, c. 543 BCE; Mahavamsa VI–VII)
nodes.notes: Prince from Lala/Vanga who landed at Tambapanni (Lanka).

nodes.name: King Pandukabhaya of Anuradhapura (r. 437–367 BCE; Mahavamsa X)
nodes.notes: United Sri Lanka and laid out Anuradhapura.

nodes.name: King Devanampiya Tissa of Anuradhapura (r. 250–210 BCE; Ally of Emperor Ashoka)
nodes.role: First Buddhist Monarch of Sri Lanka
nodes.notes: Received Ashoka's son Mahinda and planted the Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi.

nodes.name: King Dutugemunu / Dutthagamani Abhaya (r. 161–137 BCE; Built Ruwanwelisaya Stupa)
nodes.notes: United all Lanka from Ruhuna.

nodes.name: King Nyatri Tsenpo (1st Yarlung King of Tibet; Claimed Shakya/Licchavi Descent)
nodes.notes: First of the 7 Heavenly Throne Kings of Tibet.

nodes.name: Emperor Songtsen Gampo (33rd Yarlung King, 617–650 CE; Unifier of Tibetan Empire)
nodes.role: Unifier of Tibet & Sponsor of Tibetan Script
nodes.notes: Married Nepalese princess Bhrikuti and Tang Chinese princess Wencheng.

nodes.name: Emperor Trisong Detsen (r. 755–797 CE; Founded Samye Monastery with Padmasambhava)
nodes.notes: Brought Shantarakshita & Padmasambhava to Tibet.

nodes.name: Emperor Ralpacan (r. 815–838 CE; Grandson of Trisong Detsen)
nodes.notes: Expanded Buddhist translations and signed 821 CE treaty with Tang China.

nodes.name: Emperor Qin Shi Huang / Ying Zheng (1st Emperor of Unified China, r. 221–210 BCE)
nodes.role: First Emperor of Qin & Builder of Great Wall/Terracotta Army
nodes.notes: Unified Warring States China in 221 BCE.

nodes.name: Emperor Han Gaozu / Liu Bang (Founder of Han Dynasty, r. 202–195 BCE)
nodes.notes: Rose from peasant official to defeat Xiang Yu and establish Han.

nodes.name: Emperor Wen of Han / Liu Heng (Son of Gaozu, r. 180–157 BCE)
nodes.notes: Father of Emperor Jing.

nodes.name: Emperor Jing of Han / Liu Qi (Son of Emperor Wen, r. 157–141 BCE)
nodes.notes: Consolidated imperial centralization.

nodes.name: Emperor Wu of Han / Liu Che (Han Wudi, r. 141–87 BCE; Opened Silk Road)
nodes.role: Greatest Han Emperor (Zhang Qian & Sima Qian)
nodes.notes: Sent Zhang Qian to Bactria & Parthia, initiating the Silk Road.

nodes.name: Emperor Guangwu of Han / Liu Xiu (Restorer of Eastern Han, r. 25–57 CE)
nodes.role: 9th-Gen Descendant of Liu Bang & Eastern Han Founder
nodes.notes: Restored Han Dynasty at Luoyang.

nodes.name: Emperor Tang Gaozu / Li Yuan (Founder of Tang Dynasty, r. 618–626 CE)
nodes.notes: Established Tang capital at Chang'an.

nodes.name: Emperor Tang Taizong / Li Shimin (Son of Li Yuan, r. 626–649 CE; Tian Kehan)
nodes.notes: Sponsored Xuanzang's journey to India and Princess Wencheng's marriage to Tibet.

nodes.name: Emperor Tang Gaozong / Li Zhi (Son of Taizong, r. 649–683 CE)
nodes.notes: Unified the Korean Peninsula campaign in alliance with Silla.

nodes.name: Emperor Tang Xuanzong / Li Longji (Grandson of Gaozong & Wu Zetian, r. 712–756 CE)
nodes.role: Kaiyuan Golden Age Monarch (Li Bai & Du Fu)
nodes.notes: Presided over Tang cultural zenith.

nodes.name: Empress Wu Zetian (Sole Female Huangdi of China, r. 690–705 CE)
nodes.role: Only Sovereign Empress Regnant in Chinese History
nodes.notes: Consort of Gaozong; ruled in her own right as Zhou Dynasty Huangdi.

nodes.name: Emperor Song Taizu / Zhao Kuangyin (Founder of Song Dynasty, r. 960–976 CE)
nodes.notes: Ended Five Dynasties fragmentation and inaugurated the Northern Song.

nodes.name: Emperor Hongwu / Zhu Yuanzhang (Founder of Ming Dynasty, r. 1368–1398 CE)
nodes.notes: Drove out Yuan rule and established Nanjing.

nodes.name: Emperor Yongle / Zhu Di (Son of Hongwu, r. 1402–1424 CE; Forbidden City & Zheng He)
nodes.notes: Commissioned Admiral Zheng He's treasure voyages across Asia and East Africa.

nodes.name: Khan Nurhaci (Founder of Later Jin / Manchu Aisin Gioro Clan, r. 1616–1626)
nodes.notes: Created the Eight Banners; father of Hong Taiji.

nodes.name: Emperor Hong Taiji (Son of Nurhaci; Proclaimed Great Qing, r. 1626–1643)
nodes.notes: Father of Shunzhi.

nodes.name: Emperor Shunzhi / Fulin (1st Qing Emperor in Beijing, r. 1644–1661)
nodes.notes: Entered Beijing in 1644 CE.

nodes.name: Emperor Kangxi / Xuanye (Son of Shunzhi, r. 1661–1722 — 61 yrs)
nodes.notes: Compiled the Kangxi Dictionary and consolidated Tibet & Taiwan.

nodes.name: Emperor Yongzheng / Yinzhen (4th Son of Kangxi, r. 1722–1735)
nodes.notes: Centralized Qing imperial administration.

nodes.name: Emperor Qianlong / Hongli (Son of Yongzheng, r. 1735–1796)
nodes.notes: Oversaw the Siku Quanshu encyclopedia and zenith of Qing prosperity.

nodes.name: King Gwanggaeto the Great of Goguryeo (r. 391–413 CE; Hulbert Vol. 1)
nodes.notes: Expanded Goguryeo across Manchuria and the Korean Peninsula.

nodes.name: Queen Seondeok of Silla (r. 632–647 CE; Cheomseongdae Observatory)
nodes.notes: Built Hwangnyongsa Nine-Story Pagoda and Cheomseongdae.

nodes.name: King Munmu of Unified Silla (r. 661–681 CE; Nephew-Line Unifier of Korea)
nodes.role: Unifier of the Three Kingdoms of Korea
nodes.notes: Son of Muyeol; unified Silla in 668–676 CE.

nodes.name: King Taejo Wang Geon (Founder of Goryeo Dynasty, r. 918–943 CE)
nodes.notes: United Later Three Kingdoms in 936 CE.

nodes.name: King Taejo Yi Seong-gye (Founder of Joseon Dynasty, r. 1392–1398 CE)
nodes.notes: Founded Hanyang (Seoul) as royal capital.

nodes.name: King Sejong the Great of Joseon (Son of Taejong, r. 1418–1450 CE; Creator of Hangul)
nodes.notes: Grandson of Taejo; promulgated Hunminjeongeum (Hangul) in 1446 CE.

nodes.name: Turk / Japhis-Oglany (Eldest Son of Japheth in Abulghazi)
nodes.notes: Invented felt tents and ruled the Issyk-Kul steppe.

nodes.name: Taunak Khan (Son of Turk)
nodes.notes: Succeeded his father Turk.

nodes.name: Ilchi Khan (Son of Taunak)
nodes.notes: Father of Dib Bakuy.

nodes.name: Dib Bakuy Khan (Son of Ilchi)
nodes.notes: Father of Kayuk.

nodes.name: Kayuk Khan (Son of Dib Bakuy)
nodes.notes: Father of Alanja.

nodes.name: Alanja Khan (Son of Kayuk; Father of Twins Tatar & Mogul)
nodes.notes: Divided his domains between twin sons Tatar and Mogul.

nodes.name: Mogul / Mung'l Khan (Twin Son of Alanja; Ancestor of Oghuz & Borjigin)
nodes.notes: Brother of Tatar Khan; father of Qara Khan.

nodes.name: Qara Khan (Son of Mogul; Father of Oghuz Khan)
nodes.notes: Father of the hero Oghuz.

nodes.name: Oghuz Khagan (Son of Qara Khan; Epic Founder of the 24 Oghuz Tribes)
nodes.role: Great Khagan of the Oghuz Turks
nodes.notes: United the steppe nations and fathered 6 illustrious sons (Üçok & Bozok).

nodes.name: Tatar Khan (Twin Son of Alanja Khan; Eponym of the Tatars)
nodes.notes: Ancestor of the 7-generation Tatar Khans.

nodes.name: Gün Khan ('Sun', Eldest Son of Oghuz; Ancestor of Kayi / Ottomans)
nodes.notes: Forebear of the Kayi tribe from whom Suleyman Shah, Ertugrul & Osman I sprang.

nodes.name: Ay Khan ('Moon', 2nd Son of Oghuz)
nodes.notes: Bozok prince.

nodes.name: Yildiz Khan ('Star', 3rd Son of Oghuz)
nodes.notes: Bozok prince.

nodes.name: Gök Khan ('Sky', 4th Son of Oghuz)
nodes.notes: Üçok prince.

nodes.name: Dag Khan ('Mountain', 5th Son of Oghuz)
nodes.notes: Üçok prince.

nodes.name: Deniz Khan ('Sea', 6th Son of Oghuz; Ancestor of Seljuks via Kınık)
nodes.notes: Üçok prince linked with the Kınık clan of the Seljuks.

nodes.name: Seljuk Beg ibn Duqaq (10th c. CE; Founder of Seljuk Dynasty)
nodes.notes: Son of Duqaq; converted to Islam near Jand; grandfather of Tughril & Chaghri Beg.

nodes.name: Mikail ibn Seljuk (Son of Seljuk; Father of Tughril & Chaghri Beg)
nodes.notes: Father of Tughril Beg & Chaghri Beg.

nodes.name: Sultan Tughril Beg (1st Great Seljuk Sultan, r. 1037–1063)
nodes.notes: Restored Abbasid protection in Baghdad and founded the Great Seljuk Empire.

nodes.name: Chaghri Beg (Brother of Tughril; Father of Alp Arslan, d. 1060)
nodes.notes: Father of Great Sultan Alp Arslan.

nodes.name: Sultan Alp Arslan (Son of Chaghri Beg; Victor of Manzikert 1071 CE)
nodes.notes: Opened Anatolia to Turkish settlement at Manzikert (1071).

nodes.name: Sultan Malik-Shah I (Son of Alp Arslan; Patron of Omar Khayyam & Nizam al-Mulk, r. 1072–1092)
nodes.notes: Zenith of Great Seljuk power from Syria to Transoxiana.

nodes.name: Süleyman Shah (Kayi Chieftain; Father of Ertuğrul Ghazi)
nodes.notes: Led Kayi clan westward into Anatolia.

nodes.name: Ertuğrul Ghazi (Son of Süleyman Shah; Father of Osman I, d. c. 1280)
nodes.role: Bey of Söğüt & Father of Osman I
nodes.notes: Lord of the Seljuk frontier margraviate at Söğüt; father of Sultan Osman I.

nodes.name: Fénius Farsaid (Scythian King Who Studied the 72 Languages at Babel)
nodes.era: Tower of Babel Era (Lebor Gabála; Keating)
sources: Geoffrey Keating Foras Feasa ar Éirinn
nodes.notes: Founded the school of languages and fathered Nel / Niul.

nodes.name: Prince Nel / Niul (Son of Fénius; Wed Egyptian Princess Scota)
nodes.role: Linguist Invited to Egypt by Pharaoh
sources: Geoffrey Keating Foras Feasa ar Éirinn
nodes.notes: Married Scota, daughter of Pharaoh Cingris, and befriended Moses.

nodes.name: Goídel Glas / Gaedhal Glas (Son of Niul & Scota; Eponym of the Gaels)
nodes.role: Eponym of All Gaelic Peoples & Language
sources: Geoffrey Keating Foras Feasa ar Éirinn
nodes.notes: Blessed by Moses after the serpent bite; ancestor of the Milesians.

nodes.name: King Breogán (Founder of Brigantia / A Coruña in Galicia, Spain)
sources: Geoffrey Keating Foras Feasa ar Éirinn
nodes.notes: Built the watchtower from whose summit his son Íth sighted Ireland.

nodes.name: Bile mac Breogán (Father of Míl Espáine)
sources: Geoffrey Keating Foras Feasa ar Éirinn
nodes.notes: Elder son of Breogán.

nodes.name: Míl Espáine / Milesius (Galamh, Father of the Milesian Conquerors of Ireland)
sources: Geoffrey Keating Foras Feasa ar Éirinn
nodes.notes: Ancestor of Éremón (Uí Néill, Connacht, Leinster, Dal Riada) and Éber Finn (Munster, O'Brien, MacCarthy).

nodes.name: High King Éremón mac Míl (1st Milesian High King; Ancestor of Uí Néill & Scots)
sources: Geoffrey Keating Foras Feasa ar Éirinn
nodes.notes: Co-king with brother Éber Finn; ancestor of Conn of the Hundred Battles.

nodes.name: High King Conn Cétchathach ('Of the Hundred Battles', 2nd c. CE trad.)
sources: Geoffrey Keating Foras Feasa ar Éirinn
nodes.notes: Ancestor of Cormac mac Airt and Niall of the Nine Hostages.

nodes.name: High King Cormac mac Airt of Tara (3rd c. CE trad.; Lawgiver Patron of Fionn)
sources: Geoffrey Keating Foras Feasa ar Éirinn
nodes.notes: Grandson of Conn; grandfather of Niall's ancestor Fiacha Sraibtine.

nodes.name: High King Niall Noígíallach ('Of the Nine Hostages', d. c. 405 CE)
nodes.role: Progenitor of All Northern & Southern Uí Néill Dynasties
sources: Geoffrey Keating Foras Feasa ar Éirinn
nodes.notes: Father of Eógan (O'Neill), Conall Gulban (O'Donnell / St. Columba) & Lóegaire (met St. Patrick!).

nodes.name: Princess Scota (Daughter of Pharaoh Cingris; Wife of Niul & Mother of Goídel Glas)
nodes.notes: Egyptian princess married to Scythian scholar Niul; eponym of Scotland ('Scotia').

nodes.name: High King Éber Finn mac Míl (Brother of Éremón; Ancestor of Munster / Eoghanacht / Dál gCais)
nodes.notes: Ancestor of Cormac Cas -> Brian Boru.

nodes.name: Prince Ír mac Míl (Ancestral Founder of Ulaid / Ulster & Dál nAraidi)
nodes.notes: Progenitor of Cú Chulainn's Ulaid lineages.

nodes.name: Amairgin Glúngel mac Míl (First Poet & Judge of Ireland)
nodes.notes: Sang the Song of Amairgin upon landing in Ireland.

nodes.name: Prince Eógan mac Néill (Founder of Cenél nEógain / O'Neill Kings of Ailech)
nodes.role: Son of Niall of the Nine Hostages
nodes.notes: Progenitor of O'Neill High Kings.

nodes.name: Prince Conall Gulban mac Néill (Ancestor of O'Donnell & St. Columba of Iona)
nodes.role: Son of Niall; Great-Grandfather of St. Columba
nodes.notes: Ancestor of Tyrconnell & St. Columba.

nodes.name: High King Brian Bóruma / Brian Boru (r. 1002–1014 CE; Victor of Clontarf)
nodes.notes: Descendant of Éber Finn & Cormac Cas (Dál gCais); defeated Vikings at Clontarf (1014 CE).

nodes.name: King Fergus Mór mac Eirc (Founder of Scottish Dál Riata, 498 CE)
nodes.notes: Crossed from Antrim into Argyll, founding the Scottish royal stem.

nodes.name: King Kenneth I MacAlpin (Cináed mac Ailpín, 843–858 CE; 1st King of Alba/Scotland)
sources: Chronicle of the Kings of Alba
nodes.notes: Descendant of Fergus Mór; united Dál Riata and Pictland.

nodes.name: King Malcolm III Canmore (+ St. Margaret of Scotland, r. 1058–1093 CE)
nodes.notes: Married St. Margaret of Wessex (linking Scotland & England's House of Wessex!).

nodes.name: King Robert I the Bruce of Scotland (r. 1306–1329 CE; Bannockburn 1314)
nodes.role: Descendant of Malcolm III & Liberator of Scotland
nodes.notes: Won Scottish independence at Bannockburn (1314 CE); grandfather of Robert II (House of Stewart).

nodes.name: Yngvi-Freyr (Progenitor of Uppsala Yngling Kings, Prose Edda / Ynglinga Saga)
nodes.notes: Son of Njörðr; founder of the Swedish/Norwegian Yngling royal stem.

nodes.name: King Harald I Fairhair of Norway (Haraldr Hárfagri, r. 872–930 CE)
nodes.notes: Descended from the Ynglings; unified Norway at Hafrsfjord.

nodes.name: King Skjöldr / Scyld Scefing (Eponym of Danish Skjöldung Kings, Beowulf & Edda)
nodes.notes: Son of Odin in Snorri's Edda; ancestor of Danish and Viking kings.

nodes.name: King Ragnar Lodbrok ('Hairy-Breeches', 9th c. CE Legendary Sea-King)
nodes.role: Famous Viking Father of Sons of Ragnar
nodes.notes: Fathered Björn Ironside, Ivar the Boneless & Sigurd Snake-in-the-Eye.

nodes.name: King Björn Ironside (Son of Ragnar; Raided Mediterranean; Ancestor of Munsö Sweden)
nodes.notes: Led 859 CE Viking expedition to Spain and Italy.

nodes.name: King Ivar the Boneless (Son of Ragnar; Leader of Great Heathen Army 865 CE)
nodes.notes: Conquered York and Dublin.

nodes.name: King Sigurd Snake-in-the-Eye (Son of Ragnar; Ancestor of Harthacnut & Canute)
nodes.notes: Ancestor of Gorm the Old & King Canute the Great.

nodes.name: Duke Rollo / Hrólfr of Normandy (r. 911–927 CE; Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte)
nodes.notes: Norwegian noble of Jarl Rognvald's house (kin/contemporary of Harald Fairhair) who founded Normandy.

nodes.name: Duke William I Longsword of Normandy (Son of Rollo, r. 927–942 CE)
nodes.notes: Son of Rollo & Poppa of Bayeux.

nodes.name: Duke Richard I the Fearless of Normandy (Son of William Longsword, r. 942–996)
nodes.notes: Father of Richard II and Emma of Normandy (Queen of Ethelred II & Canute!).

nodes.name: Duke Richard II the Good of Normandy (Son of Richard I, r. 996–1026 CE)
nodes.notes: Father of Robert I the Magnificent.

nodes.name: Duke Robert I the Magnificent of Normandy (r. 1027–1035; Father of William the Conqueror)
nodes.notes: Son of Richard II; fathered William I of England with Herleva of Falaise.

nodes.name: King Harald III Hardrada of Norway (+ Elizabeth of Kiev, r. 1046–1066 CE)
nodes.notes: Married Elizabeth Yaroslavna of Kiev; fell at Stamford Bridge (1066 CE).

nodes.name: Brutus of Troy (Son of Silvius; Legendary Founder of Britain, Geoffrey of Monmouth)
nodes.notes: Great-grandson of Aeneas; divided Britain among sons Locrinus, Camber & Albanactus.

nodes.name: King Locrinus of Loegria / England (Eldest Son of Brutus of Troy)
nodes.notes: Eldest son of Brutus.

nodes.name: King Camber of Cambria / Wales (Son of Brutus of Troy)
nodes.notes: 2nd son of Brutus.

nodes.name: King Albanactus of Alba / Scotland (Youngest Son of Brutus of Troy)
nodes.notes: 3rd son of Brutus.

nodes.name: King Leir / Lear of Britain (Father of Goneril, Regan & Cordelia)
nodes.era: c. 8th c. BCE trad. (Geoffrey of Monmouth II.11)
nodes.notes: 8th-gen descendant of Locrinus.

nodes.name: King Beli Mawr ('Beli the Great', Progenitor of Welsh Royal Houses)
nodes.notes: Key ancestral node of British and Welsh dynastic pedigrees.

nodes.name: King Uther Pendragon (Son of Constantine; Father of King Arthur)
nodes.notes: Brother of Aurelius Ambrosius; father of King Arthur.

nodes.name: King Arthur of Britain (+ Queen Guinevere, Geoffrey of Monmouth IX–XI)
nodes.notes: Hero-king of post-Roman Britain.

nodes.name: King Hengist of Kent (Leader of Anglo-Saxon Arrival, c. 449 CE; Bede HE I.15)
nodes.notes: Jutish commander tracing pedigree to Woden.

nodes.name: King Cerdic of Wessex (r. 519–534 CE; Direct Male Ancestor of English Kings)
nodes.notes: Ancestor of Egbert, Alfred the Great & the modern British monarchy.

nodes.name: Prince Rurik of Novgorod (r. 862–879 CE; Founder of Rurikid Dynasty)
nodes.notes: Varangian prince invited to rule Novgorod in 862 CE.

nodes.name: Grand Prince Igor' of Kiev (Son of Rurik, r. 912–945 CE)
nodes.role: Son of Rurik & Father of Svyatoslav
nodes.notes: Married St. Olga of Kiev.

nodes.name: Princess St. Olga of Kiev (Regent, 945–960 CE; First Christian Rurikid Sovereign)
nodes.notes: Baptized in Constantinople (957 CE); grandmother of St. Vladimir.

nodes.name: Queen Anne Yaroslavna of Kiev (Daughter of Yaroslav; Wife of King Henry I of France)
nodes.role: Queen of France Linking Kiev to Capetians
nodes.notes: Daughter of Yaroslav the Wise & Ingegerd of Sweden; ancestral mother of Capetian France & European royalty!

nodes.name: Queen Anastasia Yaroslavna of Hungary (Daughter of Yaroslav; Wife of Andrew I)
nodes.notes: Mother of King Solomon of Hungary.

nodes.name: Queen Elizabeth Yaroslavna of Norway (Daughter of Yaroslav; Wife of Harald Hardrada)
nodes.notes: Daughter of Yaroslav the Wise who wed Harald Hardrada.

nodes.name: Grand Prince Vsevolod I of Kiev (Son of Yaroslav the Wise; + Byzantine Princess Anastasia Monomachina)
nodes.role: Son of Yaroslav & Father of Vladimir Monomakh
nodes.notes: Married Byzantine imperial princess of the Monomachos house.

nodes.name: Grand Prince Vladimir II Monomakh of Kiev (+ Gytha of Wessex, Dau. of King Harold II, r. 1113–1125)
nodes.notes: Married Princess Gytha of England (daughter of Harold Godwinson!), uniting Kievan Rus', Byzantium & Anglo-Saxon England!

nodes.name: Grand Prince Yuri Dolgoruky ('Long-Arm', Son of Vladimir Monomakh; Founder of Moscow 1147)
nodes.role: Founder of Moscow & Grandfather of Nevsky
nodes.notes: Mentioned in 1147 CE as founder of Moscow; grandfather of St. Alexander Nevsky.
